shlokas.sanskrit: अथ लोकेश्वरोत्सृष्टा तत्र कालेन केनचित् । निद्रा समभवत्तीव्रा कुम्भकर्णस्य रूपिणी ।। 7.13.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: atha lokeśvarotsṛṣṭā tatra kālena kenacit | nidrā samabhavattīvrā kumbhakarṇasya rūpiṇī || 7.13.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Now, after some time, a fierce sleep, sent forth by the Lord of the worlds and taking embodied form, came upon Kumbhakarna.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो भ्रातरमासीनं कुम्भकर्णो ऽब्रवीद्वचः । निद्रा मां बाधते राजन्कारयस्व ममालयम् ।। 7.13.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato bhrātaramāsīnaṃ kumbhakarṇo 'bravīdvacaḥ | nidrā māṃ bādhate rājankārayasva mamālayam || 7.13.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then Kumbhakarna spoke these words to his brother who was seated there: "Sleep oppresses me, O king; have a dwelling made for me."

shlokas.sanskrit: विनियुक्तास्ततो राज्ञा शिल्पिनो विश्वकर्मवत् । विस्तीर्णं योजनं शुभ्रं ततो द्विगुणमायतम् ।। 7.13.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: viniyuktāstato rājñā śilpino viśvakarmavat | vistīrṇaṃ yojanaṃ śubhraṃ tato dviguṇamāyatam || 7.13.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thereupon craftsmen, skilled like Vishvakarma, were appointed by the king; a yojana broad, gleaming white, and twice that in length,

shlokas.sanskrit: दर्शनीयं निराबाधं कुम्भकर्णस्य चक्रिरे । स्फाटिकैः काञ्चनैश्चित्रैः स्तम्भैः सर्वत्र शोभितम् ।। 7.13.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: darśanīyaṃ nirābādhaṃ kumbhakarṇasya cakrire | sphāṭikaiḥ kāñcanaiścitraiḥ stambhaiḥ sarvatra śobhitam || 7.13.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: beautiful to behold and free from all disturbance, they fashioned for Kumbhakarna, everywhere adorned with pillars of crystal and gold and of varied design.

shlokas.sanskrit: वैडूर्यकृतसोपानं किङ्किणीजालकं तथा । दान्ततोरणविन्यस्तं वज्रस्फटिकवेदिकम् ।। 7.13.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: vaiḍūryakṛtasopānaṃ kiṅkiṇījālakaṃ tathā | dāntatoraṇavinyastaṃ vajrasphaṭikavedikam || 7.13.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: That palace had stairways made of lapis lazuli and a network of little bells, gateways inlaid with ivory, and platforms of diamond and crystal.

shlokas.sanskrit: मनोहरं सर्वसुखं कारयामास राक्षसः । सर्वत्र सुखदं नित्यं मेरोः पुण्यां गुहामिव ।। 7.13.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: manoharaṃ sarvasukhaṃ kārayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ | sarvatra sukhadaṃ nityaṃ meroḥ puṇyāṃ guhāmiva || 7.13.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: The Rakshasa had it made enchanting and full of every comfort, everywhere and always granting delight, like a hallowed grotto of Mount Meru.

shlokas.sanskrit: तत्र निद्रां समाविष्टः कुम्भकर्णो महाबलः । बहून्यब्दसहस्राणि शयानो न प्रबुद्ध्यते ।। 7.13.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tatra nidrāṃ samāviṣṭaḥ kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ | bahūnyabdasahasrāṇi śayāno na prabuddhyate || 7.13.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: There the mighty Kumbhakarna, sunk in sleep, lay slumbering for many thousands of years and would not awaken.

shlokas.sanskrit: निद्राभिभूते तु तदा कुम्भकर्णे दशाननः । देवर्षियक्षगन्धर्वान्सञ्जघ्ने हि निरङ्कुशः ।। 7.13.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nidrābhibhūte tu tadā kumbhakarṇe daśānanaḥ | devarṣiyakṣagandharvānsañjaghne hi niraṅkuśaḥ || 7.13.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: While Kumbhakarna was thus overcome by sleep, Dashanana, unchecked by any restraint, went on slaying gods, sages, yakshas, and gandharvas.

shlokas.sanskrit: उद्यानानि च चित्राणि नन्दनादीनि यानि च । तानि गत्वा सुसङक्रुद्धो भिनत्ति स्म दशाननः ।। 7.13.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: udyānāni ca citrāṇi nandanādīni yāni ca | tāni gatvā susaṅakruddho bhinatti sma daśānanaḥ || 7.13.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And going to the wondrous pleasure-gardens, Nandana and the rest, Dashanana in his fury laid them waste.

shlokas.sanskrit: नदीं गज इव क्रीडन्वृक्षान्वायुरिव क्षिपन् । नगान्व्रज्र इवोत्सृष्टो विध्वंसयति राक्षसः ।। 7.13.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nadīṃ gaja iva krīḍanvṛkṣānvāyuriva kṣipan | nagānvrajra ivotsṛṣṭo vidhvaṃsayati rākṣasaḥ || 7.13.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Sporting in the rivers like an elephant, scattering trees as the wind does, and like a hurled thunderbolt against the mountains, the Rakshasa wrought destruction.

shlokas.sanskrit: तथावृत्तं तु विज्ञाय दशग्रीवं धनेश्वरः । कुलानुरूपं धर्मज्ञो वृत्तं संस्मृत्य चात्मनः ।। 7.13.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tathāvṛttaṃ tu vijñāya daśagrīvaṃ dhaneśvaraḥ | kulānurūpaṃ dharmajño vṛttaṃ saṃsmṛtya cātmanaḥ || 7.13.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When the lord of wealth (Kubera), knower of dharma, learned that Dashagriva was behaving thus, and recalled the conduct befitting their lineage and his own,

shlokas.sanskrit: सौभ्रात्रदर्शनार्थं तु दूतं वैश्रवणस्तदा । लङ्कां सम्प्रेषयामास दशग्रीवस्य वै हितम् ।। 7.13.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: saubhrātradarśanārthaṃ tu dūtaṃ vaiśravaṇastadā | laṅkāṃ sampreṣayāmāsa daśagrīvasya vai hitam || 7.13.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: then Vaishravana (Kubera), for the sake of showing brotherly affection, sent a messenger to Lanka, with counsel for Dashagriva's benefit.

shlokas.sanskrit: स गत्वा नगरीं लङ्कामाससाद विभीषणम् । मानितस्तेन धर्मेण पृष्टश्चागमनं प्रति ।। 7.13.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa gatvā nagarīṃ laṅkāmāsasāda vibhīṣaṇam | mānitastena dharmeṇa pṛṣṭaścāgamanaṃ prati || 7.13.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having gone to the city of Lanka, that messenger came before Vibhishana; honored by him in accordance with custom, he was questioned about the purpose of his coming.

shlokas.sanskrit: पृष्ट्वा च कुशलं राज्ञो ज्ञातीनां च बिभीषणः । सभायां दर्शयामास तमासीनं दशाननम् ।। 7.13.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṃ rājño jñātīnāṃ ca bibhīṣaṇaḥ | sabhāyāṃ darśayāmāsa tamāsīnaṃ daśānanam || 7.13.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And having inquired after the welfare of the king and of the kinsmen, Vibhishana presented him in the assembly hall, where Dashanana sat enthroned.

shlokas.sanskrit: स दृष्ट्वा तत्र राजानं दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा । जयेति वाचा सम्पूज्य तूष्णीं समभिवर्तत ।। 7.13.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sa dṛṣṭvā tatra rājānaṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā | jayeti vācā sampūjya tūṣṇīṃ samabhivartata || 7.13.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Beholding the king there, blazing with his own splendor, he honored him with the cry 'Victory!' and then quietly took his place.

shlokas.sanskrit: तं तत्रोत्तमपर्यङ्के वरास्तरणशोभिते । उपविष्टं दशग्रीवं दूतो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.13.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: taṃ tatrottamaparyaṅke varāstaraṇaśobhite | upaviṣṭaṃ daśagrīvaṃ dūto vākyamathābravīt || 7.13.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the messenger addressed his words to Dashagriva, who was seated there upon an excellent couch adorned with a fine coverlet.

shlokas.sanskrit: राजन्वदामि ते सर्वं भ्राता तव यदब्रवीत् । उभयोः सदृशं वीर वृत्तस्य च कुलस्य च ।। 7.13.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: rājanvadāmi te sarvaṃ bhrātā tava yadabravīt | ubhayoḥ sadṛśaṃ vīra vṛttasya ca kulasya ca || 7.13.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'O king, I shall tell you all that your brother has said—worthy, O hero, both of your conduct and of your lineage.'

shlokas.sanskrit: साधु पर्याप्तमेतावत्कृतश्चारित्रसङ्ग्रहः । साधु धर्मे व्यवस्थानं क्रियतां यदि शक्यते ।। 7.13.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sādhu paryāptametāvatkṛtaścāritrasaṅgrahaḥ | sādhu dharme vyavasthānaṃ kriyatāṃ yadi śakyate || 7.13.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'It is well; this much is enough. The store of good character has been gathered. It is well to take a firm stand in dharma—do so, if it can be done.'

shlokas.sanskrit: दृष्टं मे नन्दनं भग्नमृषयो निहताः श्रुताः । देवतानां समुद्योगस्त्वत्तो राजन्मम श्रुतः ।। 7.13.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: dṛṣṭaṃ me nandanaṃ bhagnamṛṣayo nihatāḥ śrutāḥ | devatānāṃ samudyogastvatto rājanmama śrutaḥ || 7.13.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'I have seen Nandana broken; I have heard that sages have been slain; and from you, O king, I have heard of the mobilization of the gods.'

shlokas.sanskrit: निराकृतश्च बहुशस्त्वया ऽहं राक्षसाधिप । अपराद्धा हि बाल्याच्च रमणीयाः स्वबान्धवाः ।। 7.13.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nirākṛtaśca bahuśastvayā 'haṃ rākṣasādhipa | aparāddhā hi bālyācca ramaṇīyāḥ svabāndhavāḥ || 7.13.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'And many times have I been slighted by you, O lord of the Rakshasas; yet out of childishness one's own dear kinsmen do give offense.'

shlokas.sanskrit: अहं तु हिमवत्पृष्ठं गतो धर्ममुपासितुम् । रौद्रं व्रत्तं समास्थाय नियतो नियतेन्द्रियः ।। 7.13.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ahaṃ tu himavatpṛṣṭhaṃ gato dharmamupāsitum | raudraṃ vrattaṃ samāsthāya niyato niyatendriyaḥ || 7.13.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'But I went to the heights of the Himalaya to practice dharma, and undertaking a fierce vow, self-controlled and with senses restrained, I dwelt there.'

shlokas.sanskrit: तत्र देवो मया दृष्टः सह देव्या मया प्रभुः । सव्यं चक्षुर्मया दैवात्तत्र देव्यां निपातितम् ।। 7.13.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tatra devo mayā dṛṣṭaḥ saha devyā mayā prabhuḥ | savyaṃ cakṣurmayā daivāttatra devyāṃ nipātitam || 7.13.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'There the Lord (Shiva) was seen by me, together with the Goddess; and by fate my left eye there fell upon the Goddess.'

shlokas.sanskrit: का न्वियं स्यादिति शुभा न खल्वन्येन हेतुना । रूपं ह्यनुपमं कृत्वा रुद्राणी तत्र तिष्ठति ।। 7.13.23 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: kā nviyaṃ syāditi śubhā na khalvanyena hetunā | rūpaṃ hyanupamaṃ kṛtvā rudrāṇī tatra tiṣṭhati || 7.13.23 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: '"Who might this radiant one be?"—surely for no other reason; for having assumed a form beyond compare, Rudrani (Parvati) stood there.'

shlokas.sanskrit: देव्या दिव्यप्रभावेण दग्धं सव्यं ममेक्षणम् । रेणुध्वस्तमिव ज्योतिः पिङ्गुलत्वमुपागतम् ।। 7.13.24 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: devyā divyaprabhāveṇa dagdhaṃ savyaṃ mamekṣaṇam | reṇudhvastamiva jyotiḥ piṅgulatvamupāgatam || 7.13.24 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'By the Goddess's divine power my left eye was burned, and its light, as if blasted by dust, was reduced to a tawny hue.'

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो ऽहमन्यद्विस्तीर्णं गत्वा तस्य गिरेस्तटम् । तूष्णीं वर्षशतान्यष्टौ समाधारं महाव्रतम् ।। 7.13.25 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato 'hamanyadvistīrṇaṃ gatvā tasya girestaṭam | tūṣṇīṃ varṣaśatānyaṣṭau samādhāraṃ mahāvratam || 7.13.25 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then I went to another broad slope of that mountain, and there, in silence, for eight hundred years I maintained that great vow.

shlokas.sanskrit: समाप्ते नियमे तस्मिंस्तत्र देवो महेश्वरः । प्रीतः प्रीतेन मनसा प्राह वाक्यमिदं प्रभुः ।। 7.13.26 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: samāpte niyame tasmiṃstatra devo maheśvaraḥ | prītaḥ prītena manasā prāha vākyamidaṃ prabhuḥ || 7.13.26 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When that observance was completed, the god Maheshvara, the Lord, pleased and with a gladdened mind, spoke these words there.

shlokas.sanskrit: पैङ्गल्यं यदवाप्तं हि देव्या रूपनिरीक्षणात् । प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ तपसा नेन सुव्रत ।। 7.13.27 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: paiṅgalyaṃ yadavāptaṃ hi devyā rūpanirīkṣaṇāt | prīto 'smi tava dharmajña tapasā nena suvrata || 7.13.27 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Because of the tawny hue you acquired from gazing upon the form of the Goddess — O knower of dharma, O you of excellent vows, I am pleased with you on account of this austerity."

shlokas.sanskrit: मया चैतद्व्रतं चीर्णं त्वया चैव धनाधिप । तृतीयः पुरुषो नास्ति यश्चरेव्रतमीदृशम् ।। 7.13.28 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: mayā caitadvrataṃ cīrṇaṃ tvayā caiva dhanādhipa | tṛtīyaḥ puruṣo nāsti yaścarevratamīdṛśam || 7.13.28 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "This vow has been carried out by me and by you as well, O Lord of Wealth; there is no third person who has performed an observance such as this."

shlokas.sanskrit: व्रतं सुनिश्चयं ह्येतन्मया ह्युत्पादितं पुरा । तत्सखित्वं मया सौम्य रोचयस्व धनेश्वर ।। 7.13.29 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: vrataṃ suniścayaṃ hyetanmayā hyutpāditaṃ purā | tatsakhitvaṃ mayā saumya rocayasva dhaneśvara || 7.13.29 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "This is a vow of firm resolve that was instituted by me long ago; therefore, gentle one, O Lord of Wealth, take delight in friendship with me."

shlokas.sanskrit: तपसा निर्जितश्चैव सखा भव ममानघ । देव्या दग्धं प्रभावेण यच्च सव्यं तवेक्षणम् ।। 7.13.30 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tapasā nirjitaścaiva sakhā bhava mamānagha | devyā dagdhaṃ prabhāveṇa yacca savyaṃ tavekṣaṇam || 7.13.30 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "You have been won over by your austerity — become my friend, O sinless one. And as for that left eye of yours which was burned by the power of the Goddess,

shlokas.sanskrit: एकाक्षिपिङ्गलेत्येव नाम स्थास्यति शाश्वतम् । एवं तेन सखित्वं च प्राप्यानुज्ञां च शङ्करात् ।। 7.13.31 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ekākṣipiṅgaletyeva nāma sthāsyati śāśvatam | evaṃ tena sakhitvaṃ ca prāpyānujñāṃ ca śaṅkarāt || 7.13.31 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: by the very name 'Ekakshipingala' (the tawny-one-eyed) it shall remain forever." Thus having gained friendship with him and obtained leave from Shankara,

shlokas.sanskrit: आगत्य च श्रुतो ऽयं मे तव पापविनिश्चयः ।। 7.13.32 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: āgatya ca śruto 'yaṃ me tava pāpaviniścayaḥ || 7.13.32 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: having come here, I have heard this wicked resolve of yours.

shlokas.sanskrit: तदधर्मिष्ठसंयोगान्निवर्त कुलदूषणात् । चिन्त्यते हि वधोपायः सर्षिसङ्घैः सुरैस्तव ।। 7.13.33 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tadadharmiṣṭhasaṃyogānnivarta kuladūṣaṇāt | cintyate hi vadhopāyaḥ sarṣisaṅghaiḥ suraistava || 7.13.33 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Therefore turn back from this association with that most unrighteous defiler of the family; for the gods, together with the hosts of sages, are devising a means to slay you.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवमुक्तो दशग्रीवः क्रुद्धसंरक्तलोचनः । हस्तौ दन्तांश्च सम्पीड्य वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह ।। 7.13.34 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evamukto daśagrīvaḥ kruddhasaṃraktalocanaḥ | hastau dantāṃśca sampīḍya vākyametaduvāca ha || 7.13.34 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Addressed in this way, Dashagriva, his eyes red with rage, clenching his hands and grinding his teeth, spoke these words.

shlokas.sanskrit: विज्ञातं ते मया दूत वाक्यं यस्य प्रभाषसे । नैतत्त्वमसि नैवासौ भ्रात्रा येनासि चोदितः ।। 7.13.35 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: vijñātaṃ te mayā dūta vākyaṃ yasya prabhāṣase | naitattvamasi naivāsau bhrātrā yenāsi coditaḥ || 7.13.35 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "I have understood, O messenger, the message whose words you utter. This is not you who speaks, nor is it he — the brother by whom you have been incited."

shlokas.sanskrit: हितं नैष ममैतद्धि ब्रवीति धनरक्षकः । महेश्वरसखित्वं तु मूढ श्रावयते किल ।। 7.13.36 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: hitaṃ naiṣa mamaitaddhi bravīti dhanarakṣakaḥ | maheśvarasakhitvaṃ tu mūḍha śrāvayate kila || 7.13.36 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "This guardian of wealth does not speak this for my benefit; rather, O fool, he merely makes me hear about his friendship with Maheshvara."

shlokas.sanskrit: न चेदं क्षमणीयं मे यदेतद्भाषितं त्वया । यदेतावन्मया कालं दूत तस्य तु मर्षितम् ।। 7.13.37 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: na cedaṃ kṣamaṇīyaṃ me yadetadbhāṣitaṃ tvayā | yadetāvanmayā kālaṃ dūta tasya tu marṣitam || 7.13.37 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "This that has been spoken by you is not to be forgiven by me; just as for so long, O messenger, I have endured that conduct of his."

shlokas.sanskrit: न हन्तव्यो गुरुर्ज्येष्ठो मया ऽयमिति मन्यते । तस्य त्विदानीं श्रुत्वा मे वाक्यमेषा कृता मतिः ।। 7.13.38 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: na hantavyo gururjyeṣṭho mayā 'yamiti manyate | tasya tvidānīṃ śrutvā me vākyameṣā kṛtā matiḥ || 7.13.38 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "He thinks, 'This one is my elder, my superior, and must not be slain by me.' But now, having heard my words concerning him, this resolve has been formed."

shlokas.sanskrit: त्रीँल्लोकानपि जेष्यामि बाहुवीर्यमुपाश्रितः ।। 7.13.39 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: trīँllokānapi jeṣyāmi bāhuvīryamupāśritaḥ || 7.13.39 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Relying on the strength of my arms, I shall conquer even the three worlds."

shlokas.sanskrit: एतन्मुहूर्तमेवाहं तस्यैकस्य तु वै कृते । चतुरो लोकपालांस्तान्नयिष्यामि यमक्षयम् ।। 7.13.40 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: etanmuhūrtamevāhaṃ tasyaikasya tu vai kṛte | caturo lokapālāṃstānnayiṣyāmi yamakṣayam || 7.13.40 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "This very instant, on account of him alone, I shall send those four Guardians of the World to the abode of Yama."

shlokas.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तु लङ्केशो दूतं खड्गेन जघ्निवान् । ददौ भक्षयितुं ह्येनं राक्षसानां दुरात्मनाम् ।। 7.13.41 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evamuktvā tu laṅkeśo dūtaṃ khaḍgena jaghnivān | dadau bhakṣayituṃ hyenaṃ rākṣasānāṃ durātmanām || 7.13.41 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having spoken thus, the Lord of Lanka struck down the messenger with his sword and gave him over to the evil-souled rakshasas to be devoured.

shlokas.sanskrit: एवं कृतस्वस्त्ययनो रथमारुह्य रावणः । त्रैलोक्यविजयाकाङ्क्षी ययौ यत्र धनेश्वरः ।। 7.13.42 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evaṃ kṛtasvastyayano rathamāruhya rāvaṇaḥ | trailokyavijayākāṅkṣī yayau yatra dhaneśvaraḥ || 7.13.42 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having thus performed the rite of benediction, Ravana, longing for victory over the three worlds, mounted his chariot and went to where the Lord of Wealth was.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे त्रयोदशः सर्गः ।। 13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe trayodaśaḥ sargaḥ || 13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus ends the thirteenth canto in the venerable Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana, the first poem composed by the sage Valmiki.
